$description: The Plenix layout standard: how each kind of page is laid out. This is the design system's definition; build-standards.js generates the code the applications run from it (providers/pageLayouts.js and system/layout-modes.css). Edit here, never the generated files: change a value, rebuild, and every page of that kind, in every app, follows. The composition standard (owner, 2026-10-15/16, GitHub #55) lives here too: each kind of page lists its regions in order, each region the patterns it is built from, and the fields rule (which patterns stretch a field to its column and which size it to its content). A screen is built from these patterns, never from loose components; check-system.js enforces it.

fluid.description: The page content uses the main region's full width.

contained.description: One column at the form width; the scroll area keeps the full width.

hybrid.description: Full width, with readable text and forms.

multi-pane.description: A row of panes that each scroll on their own; the page never scrolls as a whole.

focus.description: One task: the navigation and the inspector panel are hidden; the header and the footer stay.

workspace.use: Lists, grids, browse and search: most application screens (the default)

dashboard.use: An overview of widgets and sections

form.use: A form on its own page: create or edit one thing

detail.use: One record or document, with text to read

master-detail.use: A list beside the chosen item, each scrolling on its own (mail, chat)

editor.use: One task that needs all the room (image editor)

page-header.use: The page’s title and its own actions

entity-header.use: One record’s context, name, facts and its own actions (three parts)

command-bar.use: Acting on a list, and narrowing it (search, filters, sort, group, view): one bar that swaps to the selection’s commands

collection.use: The list itself: a table, cards, or a grid of media

split.use: A list beside the item chosen in it, each scrolling on its own

form.use: Collecting input: one thing to create or edit, in one or two columns

settings.use: Settings and preferences, grouped in cards

record-sections.use: A record’s content under its header: facts, activity, related lists

canvas.use: One task that needs all the room, with its tools

decide.question: Is it collecting input (create or edit one thing)?
decide.build: Form, with a chosen number of columns (1 or 2)

decide.question: Is it narrowing a list (search, filters, sort, group, view)?
Is it acting on a list or on its selected rows?
decide.build: The CommandBar, swapping to the selection’s commands

decide.question: Is it a list beside the item chosen in it?
decide.build: SplitView (side by side or stacked) with a ReadingPane

decide.question: Is it a set of commands with no list?
decide.build: A Menu (or the page header’s actions)

decide.question: Is it one record?
decide.build: RecordPage: the EntityHeader, then its sections

fields.$description: Fields (Input, Select, Combobox, SearchField, NumberInput, Textarea, the pickers) are layout-neutral: they take their natural width, and the pattern they sit in sizes them. "stretch" patterns make a field fill its column; "content" patterns size it to its content. A field anywhere else is a composition error (check-system.js). A field used alone (P-52, owner 2026-10-19) is never wider than its container (its own maximum and 100%, whichever is less) and never as wide as its placeholder or its chips; its width is chosen by what it holds, with the width prop on every field: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" (the field-width scale) | "fill". "row" patterns hold a field at a row's end: the row gives it a set share and the field fills it (ResourceList items[].field).
